entry.summary: If you enjoy fast-paced trivia games that test not only your knowledge but also your instincts, you might like the project I recently launched: GuessAnswer.com Unlike traditional trivia where accuracy is everything, GuessAnswer focuses on popularity-based guessing. Think of it as trying to predict what the majority would say, not necessarily what is objectively correct. This creates a fun mix of intuition, word association, and quick thinking. Each round gives you a question like: You type your guesses, and the game checks if your answer matches one of the top responses in the database. If it does, you score points. The challenge lies in thinking like “the crowd.” Not what you know — but what most people tend to say. Play the game instantly No downloads. No setup. Just type and play.

entry.title: Yearn yETH: How a Solver Flaw Caused a $9M Loss?
entry.summary: On November 30, 2025, Yearn’s yETH weighted stableswap pool — an LST aggregator for assets like apxETH, sfrxETH, and wstETH — was hit by a major exploit. A flaw in the pool’s fixed-point solver allowed an attacker to mint excess yETH LP tokens, break the invariant, and trigger an arithmetic underflow. By the end of the attack, nearly $9 million in LSTs and WETH had been drained. While the exploit was severe, its blast radius remained contained. The issue was isolated to the yETH ecosystem and its Curve integration. Yearn v2/v3 vaults and other core products were not affected. The team responded quickly, forming a war room and coordinating with ecosystem partners to recover 857.49 pxETH (~$2.33M), though the remaining funds were laundered through Tornado Cash. entry.title: TOON: Token-Oriented Object Notation – A Complete Guide for LLM Data Efficiency
entry.summary: Token-Oriented Object Notation (TOON) is a compact, human-readable encoding of the JSON data model, specifically designed to minimize tokens and simplify structure for Large Language Models (LLMs). It acts as a drop-in, lossless representation of JSON, allowing developers to use familiar JSON programmatically while converting to TOON for efficient AI input. TOON merges YAML’s indentation-based structure for nested objects with CSV-style tabular arrays for uniform data. Its primary strength is with uniform arrays of objects—multiple fields per row with consistent structure—achieving compactness similar to CSV, while maintaining explicit schema information for reliable LLM parsing. For deeply nested or non-uniform data, standard JSON may remain more efficient. With AI becoming more accessibl…
